subject: telescope
pitch: A brass explorer's telescope on a wooden tripod. A long tube in polished brass with leather-wrapped sections and engraved rings, a smaller finder scope on top, an eyepiece with a rubber cup, focusing knobs, and a mahogany tripod with brass fittings and a little tray holding a rolled star chart.

Now I'm sketching concrete dimensions and placement: a tripod head at roughly 0.95m height with three splayed legs made from mahogany-grained rods meeting brass feet, and a long sweep-based tube angled upward from the eyepiece toward the front, using paint helpers like grain for wood texture and simple color strings for brass to stay within color limits.

For the tripod head, I'm setting up a joint hierarchy: a root joint "stand" at the origin, a "head" joint above it, and a "tube" joint parented to head that aims toward the front of the scope so all tube parts rotate together as a rigid group. Now I'm working out the hinge points for the three tripod legs, spacing them evenly in azimuth around the head.

For each leg, I'm computing a top attachment point near the head and a splayed foot point on the ground using sine/cosine offsets at 0°, 120°, and 240°, with tapered leg sweeps and small brass shoe caps at the feet, all bound to the stand bone.

For the chart itself, I'm considering using an SVG texture on a flat plane oriented to lie upright on the tray, giving a nice star-map sheet alongside the rolled chart, using the svg import with a 256 size and texture option on the part.
